surfaceMeaning: Unmapped surface: the standard grid is a coordinate aid, not observed color or terrain.
orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF north pole (RA 0°, Dec +90°), arbitrary prime meridian and phase. No measured body pole or absolute surface attitude is claimed.
axesStatus: Illustrative equal axes at the published effective diameter; these are not three independently measured axes.
radiusMeaning: Volume-equivalent radius of the chosen illustrative equal-axis model, not a measured 3D-volume radius.
name: Salacia
periodText: About 5.494 days (131.86 hours); 2025 photometry supports synchronous rotation with Actaea.
credit: Kiss et al. (2025), EPSC-DPS conference thermal-model result; Collyer et al. (2025), synchronous rotation.
shapeMeaning: Size-constrained spherical illustration at the primary-only 838 ±44 km ALMA/NEATM estimate. This value is from a 2025 conference abstract; no resolved three-axis shape is provided.
introduction: Salacia is a large, dark Kuiper-belt world with the moon Actaea. Long-term photometry supports a synchronized binary. This grid-covered illustration uses a separately estimated primary size, not a resolved surface.

sourceSurvey.adds: New ALMA observations separate Salacia and Actaea, with distinct diameters and albedos. Conference abstract status retained.
16 years of photometry favor albedo variation and a 5.494-day synchronous rotation, rather than a triaxial explanation of the lightcurve.
JWST Salacia-Actaea spectrum is spatially blended; its 901 km discussion concerns the system and cannot set this primary’s axes.
Older 866 ±37 km estimate used equal-albedo binary partitioning; newer resolved-component result selected.

unresolved: 838 ±44 km remains a conference result; a full peer-reviewed resolved-ALMA analysis was not located in this bounded survey.
Spherical axes and pole are illustrative; the lightcurve paper favors surface-albedo variation and does not provide measured terrain.
The standard grid carries no observed albedo pattern or JWST spectral map.
